::: {.why}
The strongest raw signal you will find all phase and one of the least tradeable, which makes it the sharpest demonstration that gross performance is not the question.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report short-term reversal's gross and net information ratio and the turnover that separates them.
- Say what the signal is being paid for, and what that implies about who can run it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Build the signal and evaluate it: 1-week and 1-day reversal, both cross-sectional and neutralised. Report gross information ratio, turnover, and net information ratio at your cost model. The gross number will be the best in your book and the net number will not be.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Run the cost curve and interpret it: net information ratio against round-trip cost, with the break-even marked. Then say what the signal is: a payment for providing liquidity to whoever needed to trade, which means it belongs to whoever has the lowest costs rather than to whoever found it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add the size signal too, quickly, since it takes ten minutes and its history is the cleanest example of a published effect that decayed. Report its performance before and after 1981.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Short-term reversal and size join the book. Reversal is the book's clearest case of a signal that is real gross and dead net, and it stays in the book for exactly that reason.
:::

## Resources

- [Amihud (2002) — Illiquidity and stock returns](https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~mkearns/finread/amihud.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}
- [McLean & Pontiff (draft) — Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?](https://www.hec.ca/finance/Fichier/McLean.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Reversal and size signals evaluated, with reversal's break-even cost marked and the size effect reported before and after publication.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Short-term reversal has your highest gross information ratio and a negative net one. What is it paying for, and who can collect it?
:::
